'''Heinz-Dieter Zeh''' ({{IPA|de|tseː|lang}}; 8 May 1932 – 15 April 2018) was [[theoretical physics|theoretical physicist]] and [[professor]] [[emeritus]] of the [[University of Heidelberg]].<ref name=nachruf></ref> He is known for formalizing the theory of [[quantum decoherence]].

==Education and career==
H. Dieter Zeh was born in [[Braunschweig]] and studied physics at the [[Technical University of Braunschweig]] and nuclear physics at the [[University of Heidelberg]] as a student of [[J. Hans D. Jensen]]. At Heidelberg, he also investigated [[alpha particle]] formation in nuclei with {{Ill|Hans Jörg Mang|de}} and Zeh investigated the topic for his PhD thesis as a student of Mang. Between 1964 and 1965, Zeh was a research assistant at [[California Institute of Technology]] and in 1965 and between 1967 and 1968 at the [[University of California, San Diego]]. He later became a professor in Heidelberg.<ref name=nachruf>{{Cite web |last=Päs |first=Heinrich |date=2018-05-16 |title=Der Alte Mann und das Multiversum - Ein Nachruf auf H. Dieter Zeh |url=https://scilogs.spektrum.de/das-zauberwort/der-alte-mann-und-das-multiversum-ein-nachruf-auf-h-dieter-zeh/ |access-date=2023-09-10 |website=Das Zauberwort |language=de-DE}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Kiefer |first=Claus |journal=International Journal of Quantum Foundations |date=2018-12-29 |title=OBITUARY FOR HEINZ-DIETER ZEH (1932 — 2018) |url=https://ijqf.org/archives/5309 |access-date=2023-09-10 |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Research==
Zeh is known for his work concerning [[quantum decoherence]], described formally in his seminal 1970 paper.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Zeh |first=H. D. |date=1970 |title=On the interpretation of measurement in quantum theory |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/BF00708656 |journal=Foundations of Physics |language=en |volume=1 |issue=1 |pages=69–76 |bibcode=1970FoPh....1...69Z |doi=10.1007/BF00708656 |issn=0015-9018|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name=":0" /> He showed that the environment plays a major role in recovering the [[classical limit]] from quantum mechanics.<ref name=":0" /> In his paper he discussed applications, like explaining the emergence of [[Chirality (chemistry)|chirality]] in [[sugar]] molecules.<ref name=":0" /> In 1973, with Olaf Kübler, Zeh explained using a reduced [[density matrix]] why [[coherent state]]s are the most classical states, and why [[quantum superposition]] can never be observed.<ref name=":0" /> Zeh's works provided a solution to the [[Many-worlds interpretation#Preferred basis problem|preferred basis problem]] of quantum mechanics.<ref name=":0" />

The term decoherence was not used until 1989.<ref name=":0" /> The first experimental demonstrations of Zeh's work were given about 1996 by [[Serge Haroche]] in France and [[David J. Wineland]] in United States, who also earned the 2012 [[Nobel Prize in Physics]].<ref name=":0" /> 

Zeh's 1970 work was also one of the founding papers of the [[many-minds interpretation]] of [[quantum mechanics]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Lockwood |first=Michael |date=1996 |title='Many Minds'. Interpretations of Quantum Mechanics |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/687940 |journal=The British Journal for the Philosophy of Science |volume=47 |issue=2 |pages=159–188 |doi=10.1093/bjps/47.2.159 |jstor=687940 |issn=0007-0882|url-access=subscription }}</ref> 

Zeh also dedicated a large part of his work to [[quantum gravity]]. In 1986, he argued that gravity assumes classical properties due to environmental degrees of freedom, such as the presence of [[Gravitational wave|gravitational waves]].<ref name=":0" />
